title: Workplace Ops and Career Entry Toolkit
author: Riley Chen
content:
Summary:

This document is a consolidated toolkit for workplace operations that ties together role entry checklists, tooling access patterns, benefits orientation pointers, and the first-90-day career activation plan for new contributors at Redwood. The goal is to reduce time-to-productivity, codify predictable access provisioning, and provide a single reference for managers and new hires to run onboarding and early-career development in a consistent way.

Scope:
- Applies to all full-time employees, contractors with >3-month engagements, and interns who require system access.
- Excludes short-term vendors on a per-project basis (see vendor-engagement playbook).

Owner and expectations:
- Document owner: Riley Chen (people-ops)
- Operational owners: IT provisioning (eng-infra), Security (security-and-compliance), Hiring panel leads (hiring teams)
- SLA target for access: 95% of standard access bundles provisioned within 2 business days of start_date.

Quick start for managers (1-line action items):
1. Submit New Joiner form (People Portal) 10 business days before start.
2. Accept role-specific orientation packet and assign buddy.
3. Verify access bundle within 24 hours of orientation start.

Detailed sections

1) Onboarding flow (high level)

1. Pre-boarding (T-10 to T-1 days)
   - Manager completes New Joiner form and selects: role_band, team_template, hardware_pref (laptop/desktop), and remote_onboarding flag.
   - People-ops schedules orientation, issues welcome email and benefits primer.
   - IT kickstarts provisioning for standard bundles (see Access Matrix).

2. Day 0–7 (orientation and access verification)
   - Welcome session (People Ops): company values, benefits overview, org map.
   - Role-specific kickoff: product/engineering deep-dive, immediate deliverables.
   - Verify tool access and MFA. Run confirmation script in Section 5.

3. Weeks 2–4 (ramp and feedback)
   - Assign 30-day success goals.
   - Weekly 1:1 cadence established; first 30-day mentor check.
   - Run initial learning path modules in LMS (learning-management system).

4. Months 2–3 (career activation)
   - Establish measurable milestones for 60/90 days.
   - Perform 60-day manager check and 90-day review calibration.

2) Standard access bundles and SLA table

Bundle name | Typical recipients | Included systems | SLA (target provisioning)
--------------------------------------------------------------------------
Core Contributor | All employees and long-term contractors | SSO, email, VPN, Slack, HR portal | 2 business days
Engineering Starter | Engineers (ICs) | GitHub org, CI pipeline read, dev cluster access (staging) | 3 business days
Product & Design Starter | PMs, Designers | Product boards, analytics read, Figma org | 3 business days
Customer-Facing Bundle | CS & Sales | CRM, Zendesk, customer logs (redacted) | 2 business days
Privileged Admin | Named ops/security admins | KMS consoles, audit logs, production runbooks | 5 business days + approval

Notes:
- SLA clock starts when People-ops submits provisioning request to IT through the People Portal.
- Privileged Admin requires manager and security approval; expect manual review.

3) Access matrix (guideline table)

Role | Minimum bundle | Optional additions | Typical approver
--------------------------------------------------------------
New Engineer (IC L1-L3) | Core Contributor + Engineering Starter | Dedicated GPU lab access (if chosen), dedicated Slack channel | Team Lead
Senior Engineer (L4+) | Core Contributor + Engineering Starter + CI write | Prod monitoring access (read), release rotator role | Engineering Manager
Product Manager | Core Contributor + Product & Design Starter | Feature-flag dashboard write | Product Director
Customer Success Rep | Core Contributor + Customer-Facing Bundle | Customer production logs (read) | CS Manager
Security/IR | Privileged Admin | SIEM, KMS view | Security Lead

How to request changes:
- Use People Portal -> Access Requests -> Select bundle and justify. For bundle customizations add a short justification and list of owners.

4) Role and career ladder primer (summary)

This section provides orientation-level clarity for new joiners on how role progression is structured across engineering and product. The full competency maps live in the roles directory (linked in Related Pages).

- Bands: IC1–IC5 for engineers; PM1–PM4 for product; IC bands align to expectation matrices around: scope, technical/business impact, mentorship, and autonomy.
- Promotion cadence: Typical window is 12–18 months between-level, dependent on demonstrated impact and competency evidence.
- Promotion materials: manager-written promotion packet (impact write-up, peer feedback, selected work samples), competency matrix filled out, and calibration meeting.

5) Verification checklist and quick CLI sanity commands

Run this checklist with the new hire during Day 1 access verification:
- Can login via SSO and read onboarding intranet page.
- MFA enabled and confirmed.
- Slack access to team channels and #announcements.
- GitHub login, ability to view assigned repos.
- Access to CI pipeline read (if applicable).

Sample SSH/CLI checks (run from a terminal):
- Check VPN connectivity: curl -I https://intranet.redwood.internal/health || report to infra-support@redwood.ai
- GitHub check: gh auth status && gh repo view redwood/core || open a ticket
- CI view test: curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer $CI_TOKEN" https://ci.redwood.ai/api/v1/projects | jq '.projects[0].name'

6) First-90 roadmap template (for managers to assign)

Week 1–2: Orientation and low-risk tasks
- Accept reading list: architecture overview, security basics, console tour.
- Deliverable: merge small docs or a noop PR to learn the workflow.

Week 3–6: Deeper integration and ownership
- Pair on a feature, own a small bugfix or internal improvement.
- Deliverable: own a ticket end-to-end and demo outcome.

Week 7–12: Impact and calibration
- Drive a measurable improvement (latency, cost, or a user metric) or ship a minor feature.
- 90-day review: manager collects feedback from peers and measures against initial goals.

7) Hiring & interview panel operational checklist

Before interviews:
1. Recruiter confirms job spec and hiring rubric with hiring manager.
2. Schedule panel with cross-functional representation (engineer, product, hiring manager).
3. Panel members accept rubric and scoring guidelines.

During interviews:
1. Use standard rubric and timebox each section.
2. Collect scorecards in the candidate folder.
3. Panel convenes within 48 hours to make decision and agree on feedback.

After offer:
1. People-ops issues offer and coordinates start date.
2. Manager initiates New Joiner form and hardware provisioning.

8) Benefits orientation highlights (concise)

- Enrollment window: first 30 days for base medical, dental, vision selections.
- Time off: flexible PTO policy; manager-approved leaves in HR portal.
- Parental leave: standard policy + phased return options (see detailed policy page).

9) Escalations and critical contacts

- People-ops escalation: people-ops@redwood.ai (primary), escalation channel #people-ops-urgent
- IT provisioning: infra-provisioning@redwood.ai (SLA tracked), oncall infra phone 1-800-555-IRUN
- Security approvals: sec-approvals@redwood.ai (manual review for privileged access)

10) Maintenance and change control

- Owners must review this doc every 6 months.
- For changes that affect SLAs or security posture, notify security and eng-infra and allow 7 days for stakeholder review.

Appendix A — Example access request justification (template)
- Requestor: [Name]
- Justification: Access needed to debug customer-reported issue #1234; needs read access to production logs for triage.
- Duration: 14 days (auto-expire)
- Approver: [Manager name]

Appendix B — FAQ
Q: Who assigns a buddy?
A: The hiring manager assigns the buddy before Day 1; people-ops can assist if not assigned.

Q: What if hardware is delayed?
A: Open a ticket with infra-provisioning and request a temporary loaner device; remote reimbursement options are available.
